newsitem.title: USA: South Carolina teacher suspended, wrote on child.
newsitem.headline: South Carolina teacher suspended, wrote on child.

text.p: A first-year kindergarten teacher was under suspension Friday after writing a message on the face of a 5-year-old student.
The teacher, Phyllis Adelsflugel, wrote, "Where are my glasses?" on the little girl's face, a lawyer for the child's family said Friday.
Adelsflugel was suspended Thursday from Pepperhill Elementary, a school of 603 students, two-thirds of whom are black.
Adelsflugel wrote on the face of 5-year-old Nina Campbell Wednesday after the child repeatedly forgot to bring her eyeglasses to school.
The teacher is white, the child is black.
The child's mother, Teresa, said she believed the teacher would not have written such a message on a white child's face. Nina is afraid to return to school, the mother said.
The teacher is "very, very apologetic and understands her action was inappropriate," said school district spokeswoman Toby Smith.

Adelsflugel, who is in her first year of teaching, had written notes like "You did a good job" or "Read to me" on the faces of other students as a way to encourage children or to communicate with parents, the spokeswoman said.
